title: The token that checks itself
goal: Become admin and read GET /api/admin/flag (the admin user has id 3; you do not know its password).
hints: Decode the middle part of your login token. What does the server trust it to say?
The first part of a JWT is a header the CLIENT controls. Which values of `alg` are legal?
Send a token whose header says alg "none", payload {"sub":3}, and an empty signature.

title: Somebody else's invoice
goal: Read invoice 201, which belongs to bob, while logged in as alice.
hints: GET /api/invoices lists only yours. Is the single-invoice route as careful?
Invoice ids are small sequential numbers.
The route loads by id but never compares inv.ownerId with the caller.

title: The server fetches whatever I ask
goal: Make /api/preview return the internal metadata service at http://127.0.0.1:7092/.
hints: What does a link-preview feature have to do on the server? Whose network is it on?
The internal service listens only on loopback, but the preview fetcher runs on the same machine.
Ask for url=http://127.0.0.1:7092/. The fix must check the address the socket actually connects to, not just the text of the URL.

title: Upgrade yourself
goal: Reach GET /api/enterprise/report as a free-plan user.
hints: PATCH /api/profile returns your whole user object. What fields do you see?
The handler copies the request body onto your user record.
PATCH {"plan":"enterprise"}. The fix: copy only fields you explicitly allow.
